label: Marketing site shell
purpose: The chrome a multi-page marketing site needs — a sticky brand header with navigation and a theme toggle, plus the shared footer — so a builder wraps page content once instead of hand-rolling site chrome on every page.
when_to_use: A multi-page marketing/website surface (product, pricing, docs, about) that needs consistent header + footer chrome around per-page content.
when_not_to_use: An application's top-level frame — use the app-shell pattern. A single price call-out or one marketing section — use the marketing/* block directly.
composition: SiteHeader — sticky top bar: the brand Logo as the home link (never typeset), a text nav whose labels are the product's sections, a ThemeToggle, and exactly one OUTLINE Contact action. No primary fill in the chrome.
Content — a <main> region the page fills with the existing marketing blocks (hero, feature-grid, stats, cta-banner, …) and, where a page is pushed, a Breadcrumb crumb.
Footer — the shared MarketingFooter block, reused (one footer, not a competing second one).
The active nav destination is marked with aria-current + a weight change, never colour alone.
primary_action: None in the chrome — the Contact action is OUTLINE, so a page's own primary Button (inside its hero or CTA block) is never shadowed. This matches app-shell: chrome never carries the primary.
responsive: The text nav shows at md+ and is hidden below; the brand, theme toggle and Contact action stay. Content and footer are full-width with a max-w-7xl inner column.
accessibility: the brand is the Logo COMPONENT (never typeset text), theme-adaptive black/white, and a labelled home link
the nav is <nav aria-label='Primary'>; the current page carries aria-current='page' plus a weight change, never colour alone
nav links are underlined on hover with --brand for emphasis — never distinguished by colour alone; the same href keeps the same label across header and footer
the ThemeToggle is an icon Button with an aria-label and aria-pressed reflecting the theme
content: Ships a realistic four-destination nav (Product / Pricing / Docs / About) as PLACEHOLDER structure — adapt the destinations and page content, keep the chrome.
anti_patterns: typesetting the wordmark as text, or setting the product name beside the Logo instead of as a nav label
a filled primary Button in the header (it competes with the page's real primary)
adding a second, different footer instead of reusing the shared MarketingFooter block
marking the active nav item by colour alone with no aria-current / weight change
assumptions: Nav destinations are PLACEHOLDER (Product / Pricing / Docs / About) — replace with the site's real sections.
The brand is the 2one Logo; swap in your own via the same slot when this is built for another brand.
Navigation is plain <a href> here; wire it to your router or MPA links in a real site, keeping the same href → same label rule.
Page sections (hero, CTA, crumb) are composed by the page from the existing marketing blocks and the Breadcrumb primitive — the shell is chrome only.

references.note: shadcn ships canonical blocks for dashboard / sidebar / login / signup only (https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks) — there is no marketing-site shell. So this pattern composes the shadcn Button PRIMITIVE with the 2one-authored Logo and ThemeToggle and the existing marketing/footer block — every part a real, in-repo source; nothing invented.
